title: Connected Video Doorbell
goal: Continuously powered Wi-Fi and Bluetooth doorbell camera with 1080p30 streaming, motion detection, and two-way mono audio.

assumptions.reason: Headroom over DFRobot's reported >1 A Wi-Fi peaks plus a 3 W class-D amplifier

assumptions.value: software on the P4 from the video stream
assumptions.reason: No PIR sensor in v1; whether the P4 sustains detection plus streaming is not evaluated here

assumptions.value: GPIO with internal pull-up, button to GND
assumptions.reason: Simplest hobby wiring; debounce in firmware

designGuide.summary: A wall supply powers one ESP32-P4 board that does the heavy lifting: camera frames in over a ribbon cable, a microphone on the board, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth on its radio, and a digital audio stream out to a small amplifier and speaker. A pushbutton on one input pin is the doorbell.

flow.label: Wall supply
flow.explanation: A regulated {{psu.output_v}} V supply rated {{psu.continuous_current_a}} A. The board and the amplifier both run from it directly; there is no battery and no regulator of our own.

flow.label: Controller
flow.explanation: The FireBeetle 2 ESP32-P4 encodes video, runs the Wi-Fi and Bluetooth radio, listens on its onboard microphone, and reads the button. It makes its own 3.3 V internally.

flow.label: Camera
flow.explanation: The 5 MP camera sends frames to the board over the CSI ribbon connector, the same interface the camera was demonstrated with on this board.

flow.label: Audio out
flow.explanation: The board sends digital audio over three I2S lines to the amplifier, which turns it into speaker current for the {{speaker.impedance_ohm}} ohm speaker.

flow.label: Button
flow.explanation: Pressing the doorbell closes the contact to ground; the board reads that pin with its internal pull-up.

paths.power: Wall supply → 5 V rail → board and amplifier. No regulator is needed because the supply is already regulated and the board makes its own 3.3 V.
paths.control: Camera frames → CSI → board software → Wi-Fi stream. Audio out leaves the board as a digital I2S stream the amplifier converts to speaker current. The button pulls one input pin to ground when pressed.
paths.outcome: A streaming doorbell camera with two-way audio and a button. Motion detection and streaming latency are software behaviors; the rules check the hardware paths, not those.

parts.why: Continuous power at 5 V with headroom for the board's {{mcu.peak_current_a}} A peak plus the amplifier.
One board with the camera interface, the microphone, the radio, and enough compute to encode video. That is what makes a one-board design possible.
Supplies the video. It is the camera demonstrated with this board over CSI, so the interface is known to work.
The board outputs digital audio, not speaker-level power. This amplifier bridges that gap with up to {{amp.output_power_w}} W.
Makes the amplifier's output audible to the visitor.
The doorbell itself. Pressed, it connects the input pin to ground; the board's internal pull-up reads it, which is the assumed wiring.

decisions.title: Why one board instead of a camera module plus a separate radio?
decisions.explanation: The ESP32-P4 board already has the camera connector, an onboard microphone, and an onboard Wi-Fi and Bluetooth radio, so video, audio in, and networking all land on one part. That removes two interfaces a two-board design would need to get right and keeps the parts list short.

decisions.title: Why a separate audio amplifier?
decisions.explanation: The board's audio output is a digital I2S stream, which cannot move a speaker cone. The amplifier converts it and supplies up to {{amp.output_power_w}} W into the {{speaker.impedance_ohm}} ohm speaker. Speaker power is enough for a doorbell; the rules check that the output path exists, not how loud it is.

decisions.title: Why a wall supply and no battery?
decisions.explanation: A streaming camera and radio draw continuously; the board alone peaks at {{mcu.peak_current_a}} A. A battery would need frequent charging, so the design assumes a regulated {{psu.output_v}} V supply and skips battery management entirely.

mutations.label: Remove the camera
mutations.description: Deletes the camera module. The 1080p30 video requirement can no longer be met.

mutations.label: Remove the amplifier
mutations.description: Deletes the I2S amplifier. Speaker output is gone.

mutations.label: Remove the supply
mutations.description: Deletes the power supply. The project becomes incomplete.

mutations.label: What if the amplifier's data line is left off?
mutations.description: Disconnects DIN on the I2S amplifier while the speaker stays wired. The amplifier has clocks but no audio data, so the speaker output is silent.
